Letychiv New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Letychiv's Jewish community, first mentioned in 1581, survived a 1770 plague and a 1777 Haidamak raid, and reached a peak of 5,911 people in 1910, supporting seven synagogues and two Jewish cemeteries. In 1925, a kindergarten and Yiddish school operated as part of the 'F. Engels Jewish Children's Town.' In May 1942, a concentration camp was established here specifically for the Jews of Bessarabia, Derazhnya, and Medzhybizh — Derazhnya documented elsewhere in this collection — making Letychiv a regional collection point for multiple communities; over 7,000 Jews died in the village during the occupation in total. This is the newer of Letychiv's two documented Jewish cemeteries.
